title: Include licenses in distribution
body:
The project's licenses nor [curl's derivative MIT-like license](https://spdx.org/licenses/curl.html) are currently being distributed. This renames the project's main `LICENSE` file to `LICENSE-MIT` and adds a `LICENSE-curl` file. (Unfortunately the two licenses are legally distinct from one another.)

At the end of every tar creation command in the workflows, `$ALL_LICENSE` is used, which correlates to this:

```
env:
  ALL_LICENSE: >
    ${{ github.workspace }}/LICENSE-MIT
    ${{ github.workspace }}/LICENSE-curl
```

The `>` operator in YAML will combine the two lines with a space. `$ALL_LICENSE` cannot be quoted or else it will try to interpret both paths as one path, however this isn't an issue since `${{ github.workspace }}` will never include a space.

title: CURLFOLLOW_SAFE no longer rejects redirects to internal IPs in v2.0.0
body:
The safe-redirect SSRF guard added in v1.5.2 (#235) is accepted but has no effect in v2.0.0.

## Reproduction

Requesting `https://httpbin.org/redirect-to?url=http://127.0.0.1/` with `CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION` set to each value, via curl_cffi (which links libcurl-impersonate):

| FOLLOWLOCATION | libcurl/8.15.0-IMPERSONATE (curl_cffi 0.15.0) | libcurl/8.21.0-IMPERSONATE (curl_cffi 0.16.0) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | not followed (302) | not followed (302) |
| 1–3 | connects to 127.0.0.1 | same |
| **4 (`CURLFOLLOW_SAFE`)** | **`curl: (7) Redirect to internal IP 127.0.0.1 rejected (SSRF protection)`** | **`curl: (7) Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1:80 after 0 ms`** |
| 5+ | `setopt` rejects the value | same |

On 8.21.0 the request actually reaches 127.0.0.1 — the connection only fails because nothing listens there. With a live internal host it would succeed.

## What I checked

- `patches/curl.patch` still carries the guard in v2.0.0, unchanged from v1.5.2 — the `is_internal_ip()` helper, the `CURLFOLLOW_SAFE 4L` define, and the check in `cf_socket_open()`.
- `setopt` accepts 4 and rejects 5+, so the v2.0.0 change from `> 3` to `> CURLFOLLOW_SAFE` is in effect.
- Both `state.this_is_a_follow` and `set.http_follow_mode`, which the guard reads, exist in `lib/urldata.h` on curl 8.15.0 and 8.21.0 alike.
- The v2.0.0 release notes do not mention removing or changing this behaviour.

So the option is wired up end to end, but the rejection never fires. I could not narrow it further without building curl-impersonate myself — my guess would be that the connect path changed in curl 8.21.0 such that the patched spot in `cf_socket_open()` is no longer reached on a followed redirect, but I have not verified that.

Noticed while evaluating curl_cffi 0.16.0, which documents `allow_redirects="safe"` as SSRF protection (GHSA-qw2m-4pqf-rmpp).

title: Overhaul tests: local TLS capture, native aarch64/macOS CI runs
body:
Part of #244. The TLS signature test now captures on loopback against the local `nghttpd` server instead of external websites. Loopback packets are never fragmented, so the `dpkt.NeedData` escape hatch that silently skipped the TLS check for Chrome 124+ profiles is gone. Also fixes two tcpdump races and handles `DLT_NULL` captures, so the suite runs on macOS.

`test_http3_fingerprint` is the only test left needing internet; it is marked `remote`. A local variant needs a QUIC-aware parser in th1 — follow-up for the first checkbox of #244.

CI: native parallel test jobs for x86_64, aarch64 and arm64 macOS; DockerHub login skipped on fork PRs, where missing secrets failed the job; actions bumped to latest for the Node 20 deprecation.

title: Do not send the priority header on HTTP/1.1
body:
The impersonate profiles carry `Priority: u=0, i` in their default headers, but RFC 9218 priorities only exist on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3. Real browsers never send it on HTTP/1.1, so on a 1.1 connection the impersonation carried a header the browser would not.

Drop the priority base header in `Curl_http_merge_headers` when the negotiated version is HTTP/1.x. Covers both a pinned http_version and a server that only negotiates 1.1 over ALPN.

Adds an HTTP/1.1 regression test (the suite only had HTTP/2 servers): passes with the fix, fails without it. h2 signature tests unchanged.

Reported downstream at lexiforest/curl_cffi#785.

title: BoringSSL fails to validate Sectigo DV R36 intermediate chain on macOS
body:
## Problem

BoringSSL (bundled in the curl-impersonate dylib) fails to validate TLS connections to servers that use the **Sectigo Public Server Authentication CA DV R36** intermediate, even when a complete Mozilla CA root bundle is provided. macOS system curl (using SecureTransport) handles this same connection fine.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Using the curl-impersonate binary directly:
curl-impersonate -v https://www.gratis.com --impersonate chrome146 2>&1 | grep -i "SSL\|error\|cert"

# Expected: 200 OK
# Actual:  SSL peer certificate or SSH remote key was not OK
```

Plain system curl works:
```bash
curl -v https://www.gratis.com 2>&1 | grep -i "SSL\|certificate"
# SSL certificate verify ok.
```

## Analysis

The server sends:
- Leaf cert → `CN=*.gratis.com` (Sectigo)
- Intermediate → `Sectigo Public Server Authentication CA DV R36`
- **No root** (standard for TLS)

macOS SecureTransport builds the chain automatically from the system trust store and succeeds. BoringSSL requires the full chain including the root CA in the PEM bundle — but the root (`Sectigo Public Server Authentication Root R46`) *is* present in the Mozilla bundle.

This appears to be a BoringSSL chain-building issue rather than a missing root. The intermediate's `Issuer` field points to the root, and BoringSSL should be able to find it.

## Impact

- Any site using newer Sectigo intermediates fails with BoringSSL
- Only affects builds using BoringSSL (the curl-impersonate macOS binary uses BoringSSL)
- `--no-verify` works around it

## Environment

- curl-impersonate v2.0.0rc3 (also happened on v1.x)
- macOS 15.0 x86_64
- libcurl-impersonate.dylib built with BoringSSL

title: SIGABRT in `ssl_set_extension_order`: non-reentrant `strtok` + unbounded `order[idx]` write crashes multi-threaded Firefox impersonation
body:
# SIGABRT in `ssl_set_extension_order`: non-reentrant `strtok` + unbounded `order[idx]` write crashes multi-threaded Firefox impersonation

## Summary

`ssl_set_extension_order()` (added by `patches/boringssl.patch`) parses the `--tls-extension-order` string with `strtok()` and writes `order[idx]` with no bounds check. `strtok()` keeps its cursor in **process-global** state, so concurrent TLS handshakes in the same process corrupt each other's parse. The loop can then run past the end of the fixed-size `order` array, tripping BoringSSL's bounds assert and calling `abort()` — killing the whole process.

This only affects targets that pass an explicit extension order, i.e. **Firefox** (Chrome/Edge use `--tls-permute-extensions` instead and never enter this function).

Secondary, and arguably worse than the crash: **when it doesn't crash, it silently produces the wrong extension order**, i.e. a wrong TLS fingerprint — the exact thing the library exists to get right.

## The code

`patches/boringssl.patch`, applied to `ssl/extensions.cc`:

```c
bool ssl_set_extension_order(SSL_HANDSHAKE *hs) {
  if (hs->config->extension_order == nullptr) {
    return true;
  }
  Array<uint8_t> order;
  if (!order.Init(kNumExtensions)) {          // fixed size: kNumExtensions (28)
    return false;
  }
  for (size_t i = 0; i < kNumExtensions; i++) {
    order[i] = 255;
  }
  const char *delimiter = "-";
  char *tmp = strdup(hs->config->extension_order);
  char *ext = strtok(tmp, delimiter);         // (1) strtok: process-global cursor
  size_t idx = 0;
  while (ext != nullptr) {
    unsigned ext_index = 0;
    tls_extension_find(&ext_index, atoi(ext));
    order[idx] = ext_index;                   // (2) no `idx < kNumExtensions` guard
    ext = strtok(NULL, delimiter);            // (1) again
    idx++;
  }
  free(tmp);

  hs->extension_permutation = std::move(order);
  return true;
}
```

Two defects:

1. **`strtok` is not reentrant.** Its cursor lives in a single global (per-process in glibc). Every thread calling this function shares it.
2. **`order[idx]` is unbounded.** Nothing constrains `idx` to `< kNumExtensions`.

Neither is a problem alone. Together they crash.

## Why concurrency overflows the array

The `firefox135` profile (`bin/curl_firefox135`) passes:

```
--tls-extension-order "0-23-65281-10-11-35-16-5-34-18-51-43-13-45-28-27-65037"
```

That's **17 tokens**, and `order` has **28 slots**. A single thread parsing this alone can never exceed `idx=16` — the bug is unreachable single-threaded. Two concurrent handshakes are required:

1. Thread A: `strtok(tmpA, "-")` → global cursor points into `tmpA`. A loops, reaching e.g. `idx=15`.
2. Thread B enters the function and calls `strtok(tmpB, "-")` — the **init** form. This **resets the global cursor to the start of B's string**, a fresh supply of 17 tokens.
3. Thread A calls `strtok(NULL, "-")` → reads from the **beginning of B's string**, so A's loop continues instead of terminating.
4. Every additional concurrent handshake re-arms the cursor again. A's `idx` marches past 27 → `order[28]` on a 28-element `Array` → bounds assert → `abort()`.

Note the corruption also happens **without** a crash: A writes B's token values at A's indices, so `extension_permutation` ends up in an order that matches no real browser. With all threads on the same profile the token *values* coincide, but their *positions* don't — a silently wrong fingerprint.

## Backtrace

Real crash, `curl_cffi` 0.14.0 (bundled curl-impersonate, `boringssl-673e61fc215b178a90c0e67858bbf162c8158993`), Ubuntu 24.04 / amd64, Python 3.12, 15 worker threads sharing a process, `impersonate="firefox"`:

```
Title: python3.12 crashed with SIGABRT in bssl::Array<unsigned char>::operator[]()

#4  __GI_abort () at ./stdlib/abort.c:79
#5  bssl::Array<unsigned char>::operator[] (this=0x70b933ffdbc0, i=28)
        at .../boringssl-673e61fc.../ssl/internal.h:138
#6  bssl::ssl_set_extension_order (hs=0x70b92c1b4de8)
        at .../boringssl-673e61fc.../ssl/extensions.cc:3661
      ext_index = 15
      order = {data_ = 0x70b92c114d28 "", size_ = 28}      <-- 28 slots
      idx = 28                                             <-- writing slot 28
#7  bssl::do_start_connect (hs=0x70b92c1b4de8)      at .../ssl/handshake_client.cc:467
#8  bssl::ssl_client_handshake (hs=0x70b92c1b4de8)  at .../ssl/handshake_client.cc:1937
#9  bssl::ssl_run_handshake (hs=0x70b92c1b4de8, ...) at .../ssl/handshake.cc:651
#10 SSL_do_handshake (ssl=0x70b92c065da8)           at .../ssl/ssl_lib.cc:732
#11 ossl_connect_step2 (cf=0x70b92c1dc800, ...)     at vtls/openssl.c:4914
```

`size_ = 28`, `idx = 28` — exactly the out-of-bounds write described above, on the connect path, from a 17-token order string.

## Reproduction

Any multi-threaded process doing concurrent Firefox-impersonated TLS handshakes. Minimal shape:

```python
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from curl_cffi.requests import Session

def hit(_):
    # a NEW session each time -> forces a fresh TLS handshake per call
    with Session(impersonate="firefox") as s:
        s.get("https://example.com")

with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as ex:
    list(ex.map(hit, range(5000)))
```

Probabilistic — it needs two threads inside `ssl_set_extension_order` at once, so it reproduces faster with more threads and more new connections, and is rare when connections are reused. In production this surfaced as an abort roughly every 2-4h at ~15 threads with connection reuse, and under ~1h without reuse (handshake rate is the driver). Swapping to `impersonate="chrome"` eliminated it entirely, consistent with Chrome never calling this function.

## Platform: glibc-specific — Windows builds are structurally immune

This is an ABI difference in `strtok`, not a difference in luck:

- **glibc**: `strtok`'s cursor is a single **process-global** static, shared by all threads. Bug reachable.
- **Windows** (`msvcrt.dll` / `ucrtbase.dll`, linked by both MSVC and MinGW builds), per Microsoft's documentation:

  > Each function uses a **thread-local static variable** for parsing the string into tokens. Therefore, **multiple threads can simultaneously call these functions without undesirable effects.**
  >
  > — <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/reference/strtok-strtok-l-wcstok-wcstok-l-mbstok-mbstok-l>

On Windows every thread gets a private cursor, so `strtok` there behaves like `strtok_r`: a thread's loop always terminates at its own 17th token, `idx` never exceeds 16, and `order[28]` is never written. The crash is not merely rarer on Windows — it **cannot occur**.

Observed directly: identical code, identical `impersonate="firefox"` profile, identical 15-thread workload ran 10h+ clean on Windows, but aborts within ~1-4h on Ubuntu 24.04.

This likely explains why the bug has gone unreported despite being old: Windows users cannot trigger it at all, and Linux users get a bare `Aborted (core dumped)` with no glibc diagnostic (it's a BoringSSL bounds assert, not heap corruption) and frequently no retained core dump — so it's very hard to attribute to this function.

## Impact

- **Whole-process abort, uncatchable.** It's `abort()` in native code — no Python exception, no way to guard it from the binding layer. Every thread dies with it. For long-running scrapers/crawlers this kills the job, not the request.
- **Correlates with connection churn**, so it hits hardest exactly when a site is erroring/rate-limiting and clients reconnect in bursts — i.e. when you can least afford to lose the process.
- **Silent fingerprint corruption** even when no crash occurs, which defeats the library's core purpose and could cause hard-to-diagnose detection/blocking.
- **No glibc diagnostic** (`free(): ...` / `malloc(): ...`) is printed, because this is BoringSSL's own bounds assert rather than heap corruption — so it presents as a bare `Aborted (core dumped)` and is very hard to trace back. Also note core dumps of large Python processes are often silently dropped by `systemd-coredump` (`ProcessSizeMax`/`ExternalSizeMax`), which made this near-invisible until apport caught it.
- Affects **any** multi-threaded consumer, including `curl_cffi` users (this was found via `curl_cffi`), since the impersonation profile is process-wide code.

## Suggested fix

Make the parse reentrant and bound the write:

```c
  char *tmp = strdup(hs->config->extension_order);
  if (tmp == nullptr) {
    return false;
  }
  char *saveptr = nullptr;
  char *ext = strtok_r(tmp, delimiter, &saveptr);   // reentrant: per-call cursor
  size_t idx = 0;
  while (ext != nullptr && idx < kNumExtensions) {  // bounds guard
    unsigned ext_index = 0;
    tls_extension_find(&ext_index, atoi(ext));
    order[idx] = ext_index;
    ext = strtok_r(NULL, delimiter, &saveptr);
    idx++;
  }
  free(tmp);
```

`strtok_r` alone fixes the crash and the fingerprint corruption (each call gets its own cursor). The `idx < kNumExtensions` guard is defence-in-depth for a malformed/over-long order string — worth keeping regardless, since an order string with more than `kNumExtensions` tokens would overflow even single-threaded.

Windows note: `strtok_r` is spelled `strtok_s` in MSVC, so this needs a small shim (or `#define`) for the Windows build. Behaviour there is unchanged either way, since MSVC's `strtok` is already thread-local — but making the reentrancy explicit keeps the two platforms honest.

Related: #81 shows the compiler already warning about `ext_index` in this function.

## Environment

- `curl_cffi` 0.14.0 (also verified present on `curl-impersonate` `main` as of 2026-07-16 — `patches/boringssl.patch` still uses `strtok` with no bounds check, so 0.15.0 does not fix this)
- bundled boringssl `673e61fc215b178a90c0e67858bbf162c8158993`
- Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39), amd64, Python 3.12.3 — **crashes**
- Windows 11, same code / same profile / same 15 threads — **never reproduces** (thread-local `strtok`, see Platform section)
- `impersonate="firefox"`, 15 threads in one process

title: Add --tls-record-fragment option to split ClientHello into multiple TLS records
body:
## Summary
Add a `--tls-record-fragment` / `CURLOPT_TLS_RECORD_FRAGMENT` option that splits the TLS ClientHello into two separate TLS records at the boundary before the extensions block, hiding the SNI from deep packet inspection.
## Motivation
Censorship firewalls (e.g., GFW) inspect TLS ClientHello messages and perform SNI-based blocking. When the ClientHello is sent as a single TLS record, the firewall sees the SNI extension and immediately resets the connection.
Splitting the ClientHello into two TLS records at the record layer — before the extensions (where SNI lives) — defeats this inspection. The firewall only sees the first record (version, random, cipher suites) and cannot determine the target domain. The server reassembles the handshake normally since the split is at the TLS record level, not the handshake message level.
For detailed background on TLS record fragmentation and how it bypasses SNI-based filtering, see: https://upb-syssec.github.io/blog/2023/record-fragmentation/
## Proposed API
```c
/* libcurl option */
CURLOPT_TLS_RECORD_FRAGMENT  /* enable/disable, boolean */
CLI
curl --tls-record-fragment https://example.com
Proposed behavior
When enabled, the ClientHello is split into two TLS records during transmission:
1. Record 1: TLS record header + handshake header + fixed fields (protocol version, random, session ID, cipher suites, compression methods)
2. Record 2: TLS record header + extensions length + all extensions (SNI, ALPN, etc.)
The split only applies to the initial ClientHello (before encryption starts) and is transparent to the TLS protocol — it only affects how the bytes are framed on the wire.

title: Feature Request: TCP/IP Fingerprinting Support and OS Matching
body:
#### Issue
While `curl-impersonate` is successful at the HTTP layer, the TCP/IP characteristics (Window size, TTL, MSS, etc.) remain identical for all User-Agents. This could allow WAF and IDS systems to easily detect and block `curl-impersonate` traffic via TCP/IP fingerprinting.

#### Proposal
`curl-impersonate` should implement **TCP/IP fingerprint profiles** that correspond to the selected User-Agent or target operating system.

*   **Dynamic Configuration:** Automatically update TCP/IP parameters (TTL, Window size, etc.) based on the selected OS/UA.
*   **Consistency:** By ensuring alignment between the HTTP layer and the network layer (TCP/IP), the risk of detection will be reduced.

This enhancement will significantly improve the tool's ability to mimic real users and increase its resilience against detection.

**Reference:**
https://scrapfly.io/web-scraping-tools/device-fingerprint

title: macOS binary in v2.0.0a1 fails to locate default CA certificate bundle
body:
## Description

The macOS ARM64 binary in `v2.0.0a1` no longer resolves the system CA certificate bundle at `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`, causing all HTTPS requests to fail with:

```
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

This worked correctly in `v1.5.5`.

## Reproduction

```bash
# v2.0.0a1 - fails
./curl-impersonate-v2.0.0a1 -v https://example.com
# TLS handshake fails, no CAfile shown in verbose output

# v1.5.5 - works
./curl-impersonate-v1.5.5 -v https://example.com
# *  CAfile: /etc/ssl/cert.pem
# *  CApath: none
# *  SSL certificate verify ok.
```

Passing `--cacert /etc/ssl/cert.pem` explicitly fixes the issue:

```bash
./curl-impersonate-v2.0.0a1 --cacert /etc/ssl/cert.pem https://example.com  # works
```

## Analysis

Both binaries have `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` and `/etc/ssl/certs` present in their string tables, but only the v1.5.5 binary actually uses `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` as the default `CAfile`. The v2.0.0a1 binary's verbose output shows no `CAfile` or `CApath` at all.

This suggests a build configuration change — possibly a missing `--with-ca-bundle=/etc/ssl/cert.pem` or equivalent flag during the macOS build.

The Linux binaries appear unaffected (they have `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` compiled in and resolve it correctly).

## Environment

- macOS (Darwin 25.3.0, ARM64)
- Binary: `curl-impersonate-v2.0.0a1.arm64-macos.tar.gz`
- `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` exists and is readable

title: WS: Hardware-accelerated WebSocket masking via SIMD
body:
## Overview @lexiforest When I took cProfile captures of WebSocket send [benchmarks](https://github.com/lexiforest/curl_cffi/blob/main/benchmark/ws_bench_1_client.py), I found a severe CPU bottleneck in libcurl's code. The `ws_enc_write_payload` applies RFC 6455 XOR masking byte-by-byte and invokes `Curl_bufq_write`, capping transmit speeds: ### Changes - **SIMD Hardware Acceleration:** To fix this, I added AVX-512, AVX2, and ARM NEON vectorized XOR masking. Fallback scalar paths are optimized and gated safely behind macros for runtime dispatch, maintaining static-binary portability. I've aligned the XOR buffer (`xbuf`) to 64-byte cache lines to reduce memory latency penalties. - **Increased Buffer Size:** Increased `WS_CHUNK_SIZE` from 64KB to 128KB to reduce `recv()`/`send()` syscall overhead. - **State Machine Hardening:** * Fixed an issue in `ws_flush` where partial-write progress was dropped if the socket returned `CURLE_AGAIN` on the same cycle, preventing frame corruption. * Fixed `ws_send_raw_blocking` so that it accurately reports partial bytes sent to the callback layer if a connection dies mid-stream. * Improved End-of-Stream validation in `ws_cw_write` to ensure the decoder is cleanly reset before accepting stream termination. This PR accompanies the https://github.com/lexiforest/curl_cffi/pull/749 PR. ### Impact Once the patch is applied WebSocket transmit speeds are massively improved. They are no longer CPU-bound and huge speed improvements are visible (more than 10x on my server). The send side now provides multi-gigabit throughput:
In fact, the bottleneck is now AIOHTTP!
When acting as the receiving server, AIOHTTP is CPU pinned at 100%. AVX-512 can result in downclocking in some CPUs, but the clock drop should still leave us with good performance. The best part is that the patches are done in a highly portable way, so if your CPU does not support AVX-512/AVX2/NEON SIMD instructions, it will fall back to a fast scalar loop that's still much faster than the original code. CPU feature detection is done via runtime dispatch so the library can seamlessly statically link and run like normal. No additional compiler flags or build step changes are needed.

title: Add type information to Python test code
body:
Follow-up from #249.

The Python test helpers have grown enough that they should carry explicit type information. New Python code should use annotations where practical, especially around async fixtures, request dictionaries, parsed HTTP/3 settings, and QUIC transport parameter structures.

Suggested scope:

- add type annotations to the shared Python test helpers in `tests/test_impersonate.py`
- introduce small typed structures or aliases for HTTP/3 request data, settings entries, and QUIC transport parameters where that improves readability
- keep the runtime behavior unchanged
- consider adding a lightweight static type check target if it fits the test tooling

This is cleanup rather than a blocker for the HTTP/3 test coverage, but it would make future Python test changes easier to review and maintain.

title: TLS Fingerprint difference with Chrome 146
body: Hello, While running some benchmarks and tests, I've discovered that the TLS fingerprint does not fully match Chrome at least from version 145-147, there could be more but I only tested those versions. It's close but with the differences, its not quite Chrome. I also tested Chromium and found that it had the same fingerprint as Chrome, so presumably any browser which is Chromium based will also have this difference. To replicate: I used Curl-CFFI to send a GET request to `http://api.gemini.com/` with `impersonate="chrome146"` while I had Wireshark open. I then opened Chrome 146 & 147 and loaded the same page. I then filtered the Client Hello in Wireshark and compared them. The same difference is visible on any website and OS. I did not test HTTP/3. From this Cloudflare article: https://blog.cloudflare.com/ja4-signals/ I can see 3 key differences in the Wireshark capture: - The number of extensions are different: 15 vs 16 extensions - The JA4_c hash is different as a result of the first point - The first ALPN value is `h1` instead of `h2` which should be the default for HTTP/2 The missing extension is application_settings (17613): https://chromestatus.com/feature/5149147365900288 I see that Go's uTLS library has this extension implemented, here is the issue: https://github.com/refraction-networking/utls/issues/330 uTLS PR: https://github.com/refraction-networking/utls/pull/333 Can this be implemented please? Thank you for maintaining this library.

title: SSRF Protection: Include Multicast and Reserved IP ranges in `--location-safe`
body:
**Description:**
The SSRF protection provided by the `--location-safe` option should be expanded. In addition to the existing private network (RFC 1918) checks, the following range should also be included in the blocklist:

*   **224.0.0.0 - 255.255.255.255** (Multicast, Reserved, and Broadcast addresses)

**Justification:**
Addresses in this range (especially Multicast) are not legitimate targets for standard HTTP traffic. An attacker can use redirects to target these addresses to probe internal services (e.g., mDNS, SSDP) or manipulate network devices. Blocking these ranges will ensure a more robust and secure defense against SSRF attacks.

title: HTTP/3 Extension Order Issue in H3 Connections
body:
https://github.com/lexiforest/curl-chrome/blob/7b5f3b36d0e120c26e01c5df3c75a0a3478c1e3f/lib/vtls/openssl.c#L4697-L4700
```C
    char *ext_order = (peer->transport == TRNSPRT_QUIC
                       && data->set.str[STRING_HTTP3_TLS_EXTENSION_ORDER])
                      ? data->set.str[STRING_HTTP3_TLS_EXTENSION_ORDER]
                      : data->set.str[STRING_TLS_EXTENSION_ORDER];
```
When the HTTP/3 extension order value is defined as null, the system incorrectly uses the H2 extension order settings for H3 connections.
The following part of the code should be removed: `&& data->set.str[STRING_HTTP3_TLS_EXTENSION_ORDER]`

BUG: `firefox144` and `firefox147` impersonation presets use mismatched `rv:` version in User-Agent strings
body:
### Summary

In Firefox User-Agent strings, the **`rv:<version>` should match `Firefox/<version>`**.

Currently, two Firefox impersonation presets, `firefox144` and `firefox147`, exhibit a version mismatch in `User-Agent` header. Both are hardcoded with `rv:135.0` while claiming to be Firefox 144/147.

### Observed Behavior

The User-Agent strings are currently set as follows:

- **firefox144**: `... rv:135.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/144.0`, 
- **firefox147**: `... rv:135.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/147.0`

Note that the **`rv:135.0`** value doesn't align with the trailing **`Firefox/144.0`** and **`Firefox/147.0`** versions. 

### Expected Behavior

The rv version should be synchronized with the Firefox version:

- `firefox144` should use `rv:144.0 ... Firefox/144.0`
- `firefox147` should use `rv:147.0 ... Firefox/147.0`

### Impact

Such an "impossible" UA string creates a unique signature that makes the impersonation attempt backfire, pinpointing the user rather than hiding them.


### Suggested Fix / Code Location

The hardcoded User-Agent `firefox144` and `firefox147` in `impersonations[]` presets in `lib/impersonate.c` need to be updated:

https://github.com/lexiforest/curl-chrome/blob/6da216c2b8a99f73d540bea31370e6fb6b657857/lib/impersonate.c#L1221-L1221
https://github.com/lexiforest/curl-chrome/blob/6da216c2b8a99f73d540bea31370e6fb6b657857/lib/impersonate.c#L1288-L1288

title: Every other request fails, closed by server due to sending frequent HTTP2 priority frames
body:
This happens when downloading more than one file from either a Cloudflare proxy or nginx web server (and possibly others).

I've reproduced it on the latest Docker image, my own Docker build from the main branch, as well building the release version from the Arch Linux AUR. It doesn't happen with stock curl. Terminal output is below.

I looked at the traffic in Wireshark. After a short while, curl sends a burst of dozens of HTTP 2 PRIORITY frames within a couple seconds. This seems to cause the server to close the connection (by sending a GOAWAY frame with ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM error).

From what I can tell, HTTP 2 priority frames are no longer used. I created a quick patch that removes the code that sends them. This fixes the problem for me. The patch is below.

I initially tried only reverting curl-impersonate's changes to the priority code and leaving the call to `nghttp2_submit_priority`, however that only improved the problem with my nginx server, but not Cloudflare. I'm not sure why stock curl still works fine, maybe there's an interaction with code somewhere else in curl-impersonate's patches.

I'm not sure how disabling priority frames affects fingerprinting. Although I imagine if browsers no longer send PRIORITY frames, it should improve stealth.

title: Add ppc64le cross-build support
body:
Follow the existing Linux alt-arch jobs and add a Zig cross-build for powerpc64le-linux-gnu on Ubuntu.

ppc64le still needs Chromium's downstream BoringSSL POWER support. Use Fedora's unchanged patch pair from chromium commit c710b35d38ebe3e04f8880bdb3191406f6273441:

https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/chromium/raw/c710b35d38ebe3e04f8880bdb3191406f6273441/f/0001-Add-PPC64-support-for-boringssl.patch https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/chromium/raw/c710b35d38ebe3e04f8880bdb3191406f6273441/f/0002-Add-PPC64-generated-files-for-boringssl.patch

Makefile.in adds the ppc64le-specific glue needed to use those patches unchanged: stage BoringSSL in the Chromium-style
third_party/boringssl/src layout they expect, and wrap the BoringSSL C++ compiler so -Wno-missing-prototypes applies to cpu_ppc64le.cc without editing the downstream patches.

Tested with the same Ubuntu 24.04 + Zig 0.14.0 cross-build flow used in CI:
./configure --prefix=/tmp/install --enable-static --disable-shared --host=powerpc64le-linux-gnu --with-ca-path=/etc/ssl/certs --with-ca-bundle=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt make build
make checkbuild
make install-strip

title: Add CURLOPT_SSL_SIG_HASH_ALGS_H3 for per-protocol signature algorithms
body:
sig_hash_algs is broken for H3 impersonation.

Chrome uses different TLS signature algorithm lists for TCP vs QUIC. On TCP, `ssl_client_socket_impl.cc` calls `SSL_set_verify_algorithm_prefs()` with 8 algorithms, no SHA-1. On QUIC, nobody calls it. Not Chrome, not quiche, nobody. So BoringSSL's default kicks in from `ssl/extensions.cc` which includes `rsa_pkcs1_sha1` (0x0201) as the 9th entry.

We captured this from real Chrome 146.0.7680.80 on Linux. Same browser, same session, same machine:

- H2: `[1027, 2052, 1025, 1283, 2053, 1281, 2054, 1537]` — 8 sig algs, no SHA-1
- H3: `[1027, 2052, 1025, 1283, 2053, 1281, 2054, 1537, 513]` — 9 sig algs, SHA-1 at the end

Right now `sig_hash_algs` is a single field applied to both TCP and QUIC via `Curl_ossl_ctx_init()`. A detection server just compares the `signature_algorithms` extension between H2 and H3 from the same client. Real Chrome: different. curl-impersonate: identical.

This adds `sig_hash_algs_h3` to the impersonate struct and `CURLOPT_SSL_SIG_HASH_ALGS_H3`. When set, `openssl.c` uses it for QUIC connections (`peer->transport == TRNSPRT_QUIC`). Falls back to `sig_hash_algs` if not set, so nothing breaks for existing targets.

Also adds `chrome146_linux` with both fields set and verified against real Chrome.

Closes #229

title: Single sig_hash_algs for h2 vs h3
body:
sig_hash_algs is broken for H3 impersonation.

Chrome sets up TLS differently for TCP vs QUIC. On TCP (H2), Chromium explicitly strips SHA-1 from the signature algorithms list in net/socket/ssl_client_socket_impl.cc - it calls SSL_set_verify_algorithm_prefs() with a hardcoded list of 8 algorithms, no SHA-1. The comment literally says "Disable SHA-1 server signatures."

On QUIC (H3), nobody calls SSL_set_verify_algorithm_prefs. Not Chromium, not quiche, nobody. So BoringSSL's default kicks in from ssl/extensions.cc which includes rsa_pkcs1_sha1 (0x0201) at the bottom with the comment "For now, SHA-1 is still accepted but least preferable."

Result: real Chrome sends 8 sig algs on H2 and 9 on H3. We verified this by capturing from Chrome 146 on the same machine, same session. H2 gets [1027, 2052, 1025, 1283, 2053, 1281, 2054, 1537]. H3 gets the same list plus 513 (rsa_pkcs1_sha1) at the end. Every single time.

curl-impersonate can't replicate this because sig_hash_algs is a single field in the impersonate struct. It gets applied through Curl_ossl_ctx_init() which is called by both the TCP path (openssl.c) and the QUIC path (vquic-tls.c -> Curl_vquic_tls_init -> Curl_ossl_ctx_init). Same SSL_CTX setup, same sig alg list, both protocols.

So you're stuck. Set sig_hash_algs to match H2 (no SHA-1) and your H3 is wrong. Set it to match H3 (with SHA-1) and your H2 is wrong. A detection server just compares the signature_algorithms extension between a client's H2 and H3 connections. Real Chrome: different. curl-impersonate: identical.

Fix needs a separate sig_hash_algs_h3 option

title: Inconsistency in Header Injection and Decoding when using `CURL_IMPERSONATE` Environment Variable
body:
**Description:**
There is a functional discrepancy between using the `--impersonate` command-line flag and the `CURL_IMPERSONATE` environment variable.

**Issues Observed:**
1.  **Header Mismatch:** When using the `--impersonate "chrome142"` flag, headers and the User-Agent are correctly spoofed. However, when using the `CURL_IMPERSONATE=chrome142` environment variable, the User-Agent does not change as expected.
2.  **Decoding Failure(zstd):** Automatic response decoding works correctly with the flag but fails to trigger when the environment variable is used.

**Comparison:**

*   **Correct Behavior (Flag):**
    ```bash
    curl-impersonate --compressed --impersonate "chrome142" https://example.com/
    ```
*   **Incorrect Behavior (Env Var):**
    ```bash
    CURL_IMPERSONATE=chrome142 curl-impersonate https://example.com/
    ```

**Expected Behavior:**
The environment variable should provide the same header configurations and decoding functionality as the corresponding command-line arguments. This inconsistency prevents seamless integration in environments where setting variables is preferred over modifying command strings.

title: Question: Does `curl-impersonate` support E-SNI / ECH?
body:
Hi there,

I am currently exploring `curl-impersonate` for use cases involving privacy-preserving network traffic. I would like to inquire whether the tool currently supports **E-SNI (Encrypted Server Name Indication)** or its more recent evolution, **ECH (Encrypted Client Hello)**.

Since `curl-impersonate` is specifically designed to mimic the TLS/HTTP fingerprints of modern browsers, and browsers like Firefox and Chrome have been moving toward implementing these standards to prevent SNI-based filtering/leaking, I was wondering:

1.  Is E-SNI/ECH support currently available in any of the provided builds (e.g., Chrome or Firefox impersonation)?
2.  If not, is this feature on the roadmap for future releases?

This would be a very useful feature for accurately simulating modern browser behavior in environments where encrypted handshakes are expected.

Thank you for your work on this project

title: [Feature] Make it build on Android (Termux)
body:
[Makefile.in.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24249100/Makefile.in.txt)

Using this `Makefile.in`, the project compiles without error in Termux.

However, ECH needs to be turned off to work. (not sure how to enable on Android)

The BoringSSL library needs to be compiled with 

```
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON -DOPENSSL_NO_ASM=ON -DBORINGSSL_SHARED_LIBRARY=ON -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=1
```
(this is in the `Makefile.in` above)
in order to successfully compile curl-impersonate on Android. 
If you try and force shoving down the statically compiled BoringSSL libraries, you will get "discouraged" by libtool first with the warning that the library is not portable, then full stop comes to the compilation.

But even if you complete the compilation by the shared libraries, it'll try resolving them into the system's libraries. You can override this using the `LD_PRELOAD` trick.

So to perform this, you'll need the BoringSSL libraries you've used during compilation then do 

```
LD_PRELOAD=libcrypto.so:ssl.so curl-impersonate
```
Then, it should work just as usual, but with every launch you'll need the `LD_PRELOAD` addition before the executable's name. 
You also need to get a PEM from https://curl.se/docs/caextract.html and pass it using `--cacert cacert.pem`
To persistently create a shortcut that makes it ready to use, you'll likely going to need a wrapper that does it.

Also, do not attempt to replace the system libs, you'll break the whole coreutils suite if you'll try replacing the prefix's `libcrypto` library, from which you can only recover from using the failsafe launch or starting from scratch.

title: Multipart boundary not impersonated
body:
## Summary
Multipart boundaries generated by `curl_cffi` doesn't follow the pattern generated by Chromium-based browsers. Below are the examples demonstrating the differences of boundary patterns:

## curl_cffi
```py
import curl_cffi
import curl_cffi.requests

multipart = curl_cffi.CurlMime()
multipart.addpart(
  name = 'file',
  filename = 'testfile.txt',
  data = b'content'
)
curl_cffi.requests.post('http://127.0.0.1/upload', multipart = multipart, impersonate = 'chrome')
```
Generates the following HTTP request -
```http
POST /upload HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=------------------------7HNeDYLJcCfGxjFhnIdObM

--------------------------7HNeDYLJcCfGxjFhnIdObM
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="testfile.txt"
Content-Type: text/plain

content
--------------------------7HNeDYLJcCfGxjFhnIdObM--

```

## Chromium
```html
<html>
  <head></head>
  <body>
    <form action="http://127.0.0.1/upload" method="POST" enctype="multipart/form-data">
      <input type="file" name="file">
      <input type="submit">
    </form>
  </body>
</html>
```
Generates the following HTTP request -
```http
POST /upload HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundarypxnYIQZlLJZBSUSX

------WebKitFormBoundarypxnYIQZlLJZBSUSX
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="testfile.txt"
Content-Type: text/plain

content
------WebKitFormBoundarypxnYIQZlLJZBSUSX--

```

title: tls13 cipher list
body:
using profile chrome136.

I've got a site that uses http3 and sits behind CF.

libcurl-impersonate fails the fingerprint unless i force tls13 only via CURLOPT_SSL_VERSION = TLSv1_3.

the default is tls12 | MAX which does tls13 with tls12 fallback.

i think what is happening is that the initial http3 handshake used a different (tls13 specific) cipher suite and forcing TLSv13 actually just uses the default curl tls13 cipher suite which happens to pass the fingerprint check.

curl has CURLOPT_TLS13_CIPHERS but it fails NOT_BUILT_IN if i try to use it to.

my thought is that probably the impersonate profile could use a .tls13_ciphers field that gets passed to CURLOPT_TLS13_CIPHERS so that http3 initiated sessions can be easily used.

title: remove: auto-prepend of 'Host' header
body:
This PR addresses https://github.com/lexiforest/curl-impersonate/issues/165.

It prevents curl from prepending an automatic `Host:` header when one is already explicitly provided. Previously, even if the `Host:` header was passed in manually, curl would still insert its own version at the top of the request, breaking the intended header order.

The patch changes the logic to skip generation of the internal `Host:` header if a user-defined one is detected. It sets `aptr->host = NULL` to avoid prepending it and removes the guard that previously suppressed the user-supplied header when the internal one was set.

Tested successfully by building locally according to INSTALL.md.

Let me know what you think of this PR and if it's mergeable. I'm not very experienced with C, so open to improvements if needed.

title: Host header is always prepended even when explicitly set
body:
When using `curl-impersonate` (via `curl-cffi`), I’m seeing curl prepend a `Host:` header to the very top of the request, even though I’m already providing one manually.

The raw headers that are being passed to `CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER` are correct, but curl still injects its own `Host:` ahead of them, altering the order. This breaks header order in subtle ways and makes exact request reproduction impossible in some cases.

Raw headers passed to `CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER` by `curl-cffi`:
```
[b'MA-App-Version: 34837196', b'MA-OS-Version: 30', b'MA-Platform: 10FT-ANDROID-TV', b'platform: 10FT-ANDROID-TV', b'Install-ID: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', b'Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8', b'Content-Length: 140', b'Host: gateway.moviesanywhere.com', b'Connection: Keep-Alive', b'Accept-Encoding: gzip', b'User-Agent: okhttp/4.12.0', b'Accept:', b'Expect: ']
```

Sniffed request:
```
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: gateway.moviesanywhere.com <-- prepended
MA-App-Version: 34837196
MA-OS-Version: 30
MA-Platform: 10FT-ANDROID-TV
platform: 10FT-ANDROID-TV
Install-ID: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 140
Connection: Keep-Alive
Accept-Encoding: gzip
User-Agent: okhttp/4.12.0
```

Original/ Goal:
```
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
MA-App-Version: 34837196
MA-OS-Version: 30
MA-Platform: 10FT-ANDROID-TV
platform: 10FT-ANDROID-TV
Install-ID: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 140
Host: gateway.moviesanywhere.com
Connection: Keep-Alive
Accept-Encoding: gzip
User-Agent: okhttp/4.12.0
```

It would be amazing if your fork could suppress prepending `Host:` when one is already explicitly provided. I would propose my own PR, but I'm not fluent in C and tbh I don't trust myself a bit lol.

Thanks in advance!

title: Add support for building binaries for Windows on ARM
body:
PR description:
- The main motive of this PR is to add support for [curl_cffi](https://github.com/lexiforest/curl_cffi) python wheels for Windows on ARM(WoA).
- As part of this effort, currently curl_cffi internally [uses curl_impersonate](https://github.com/lexiforest/curl_cffi/blob/main/libs.json#L8) binary for building its wheels - Currently, the releases contains only Windows x64/x86 builds.
- The PR add support for building curl_impersonate on Windows on ARM natively with the following changes:
  - Added new native Windows on ARM github runner
  - Changed base python version from 3.10 ---> 3.11, since Python 3.10 is not available for WoA at this point.
  - The boringssl does not have implementation for arm with assembly which causing building errors by picking up wrong implementation from x86 - To fix this, I added cmake flag to avoid building assemblies on WoA
- Please feel free to ping if you have any suggestions/guidance to make curl_cffi and curl_impersonate more accessible for this growing platform

title: Add new option `--proxy-credential-no-reuse`
body:
I assume this is the way to submit changes since https://github.com/lexiforest/curl-chrome-archive was archived.

Two issues that I attempt to address as discussed in: https://github.com/lexiforest/curl-impersonate/issues/146: 
a) SSL session resumption/reuse from different IP addresses after proxy "rotation" via changing the credentials (mainly username)
b) Connection reuse after the same as the above

For the first case, we include some proxy information inside the ssl_peer_key which means that if credentials change, the entire hash will change and thus the session will not be resumed. 
But if we switch back to the original credentials, it can still be resumed.

For the second case, there is a simple comparison in `url_match_proxy_use` in `lib/url.c` that checks the credentials for an exact match.

This isn't optimal and ideally these should be two separate switches (one for connection and one for SSL) but I haven't been able to think of a scenario where you'd want to opt into one and not the other.

This should (hopefully) close 
https://github.com/lexiforest/curl_cffi/issues/369 
https://github.com/lexiforest/curl_cffi/issues/308
and my issue https://github.com/lexiforest/curl-impersonate/issues/146 (I probably will extract the 0-RTT stuff and open another issue when this gets merged).

Also does https://github.com/curl/curl/pull/17408 fix any of these?
https://github.com/lexiforest/curl_cffi/issues/302
https://github.com/lexiforest/curl_cffi/issues/319


Let me know if any changes need to be made.

title: Session cache handling & improvements
body:
If I understand correctly, the CURL patch enables toggling the advertisement of TLS session tickets in the TLS extensions during the handshake. 
This is done before [calling the corresponding BoringSSL functions](https://github.com/lexiforest/curl-impersonate/blob/main/patches/curl.patch#L3928). 

Now here is something I have a few questions about:

If we advertise session tickets in the ClientHello, then depending on a) whether the server supports this extension and b) TLS version the server will either (for [TLSv1.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5077#section-3.3)) include a session ticket extension in the ServerHello and then issue a NewSessionTicket message or (for [TLSv1.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8446#section-4.6.1)) send the NewSessionTicket message at some time after receiving the client Finished message.

The information inside that message is discarded/not used in the current implementation according to my understanding.

e.g.
``` 
> curl  --tls-session-ticket --http2 https://nghttp2.org
> curl  --tls-session-ticket --http2 https://nghttp2.org
```
If we assume the aforementioned exchange occurred properly, then the 2nd invocation here will NOT include the session ticket.

This is conformant behavior according to RFC 8446
`The client **MAY** use this PSK for future handshakes by including the
   ticket value in the "pre_shared_key" extension in its ClientHello`

But browsers will most likely use the session data if it meets their requirements (e.g. [chrome](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/main/net/ssl/ssl_client_session_cache.cc#L63)).

Both CURL and BoringSSL have their own session caches. 

In case of BoringSSL, there is only support for an external cache for clients, see [here](https://github.com/google/boringssl/blob/673e61fc215b178a90c0e67858bbf162c8158993/include/openssl/ssl.h#L2059) and CURL [sets the cache to external ](https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/9fc05357ef91e9d5a3c6662a30a67c96cac0b2e5/lib/vquic/curl_ngtcp2.c#L2357) anyway.

CURL only supported a [TLS Session-ID cache which was in-memory only](https://everything.curl.dev/internals/caches.html#tls-session-id-cache) (that wouldn't be sufficient nowadays) until v8.12, so it was destroyed in the example above.
The [new implementation ](https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html#--ssl-sessions) uses a file provided via `--ssl-sessions` for CLI, and a [few functions](https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/curl-8_13_0/include/curl/curl.h#L3278C1-L3278C13) for the library. (see also: https://github.com/curl/curl/discussions/15684, https://github.com/curl/curl/pull/15924). 

I can neither prove or disprove that this is used for fingerprinting purposes, but I assume so because it's straightforward. 
Any interested service would *know* they have sent a NewSessionTicket message and they *know* the behavior of genuine browsers and that the observed behavior differs. This is most likely done for a series of requests to the same server.

For the use case of https://github.com/lexiforest/curl_cffi, the cache is not destroyed, but there might be another issue:

If one were using multiple proxy servers (namely via the still prevalent HTTP CONNECT),  CURL will re-use the session since it checks for options [concerning the destination ](https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/curl-8_13_0/lib/vtls/vtls_scache.c#L448) regardless of which proxy was used. This is most likely very easy to detect.

I am not really a fan of using a file for persistent storage and would prefer using e.g. a persistent shared memory space, but that'd be more complex.

Motivation behind this: 

The most recent chrome stable release (v138.0.7204.33+) can enable/use [TLSv1.3 early data](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8446#section-2.3) (see [here](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7679408?sjid=4094753554462597130-EU#chromeBrsrN138)).
It can be turned on/off (via chrome flags `chrome://flags/#enable-tls13-early-data` or [policies](https://chromeenterprise.google/policies/#TLS13EarlyDataEnabled)).
CURL supports this since v8.12 (https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html#--tls-earlydata) and according to the docs it's enabled when building with GnuTLS. But it per definition requires a persistent storage across multiple executions. 
Additionally, probably have to patch [this guard](https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/curl-8_13_0/lib/vtls/openssl.h#L55) and also check how many bytes chrome actually writes when it uses this mode.


In summary:
1. Set `USE_SSLS_EXPORT` during build and either delegate providing the ssl session cache file to the user, hardcode it or use the library functions to implement a persistent storage in some other way
2. Someone should probably verify the interaction of switching proxies with the session cache experimentally, I only checked the code. If it in fact behaves as suspected, most likely some information on the used proxy should be included in the ssl_peer_key.


I am new to this project, so let me know if I overlooked or misunderstood something.

title: [Bug] Docker image `v1.0.2` gives `"curl": executable file not found in $PATH: unknown` and `error while loading shared libraries: libc++.so.1`
body:
**Problem 1**

It gives an error when using `lexiforest/curl-impersonate:v1.0.2`.

```shell
$ docker run --rm -it lexiforest/curl-impersonate:v1.0.2

docker: Error response from daemon: failed to create task for container: failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init: exec: "curl": executable file not found in $PATH: unknown

Run 'docker run --help' for more information
```

**Problem 2**

When accessing the shell and manually try to execute `curl-impersonate` or `curl_chrome136`, it gives another error.

```shell
$ docker run --rm -it lexiforest/curl-impersonate:v1.0.2 /bin/bash

root@97a2c572fda5:/usr/local/bin# curl-impersonate --help
curl-impersonate: error while loading shared libraries: libc++.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

---

**Sidenote**

I'm currently still using the following workaround, which is downloading and extracting from release directly, which works fine (also for `v1.0.2`)

```Dockerfile

ARG CURL_IMPERSONATE_VERSION='v1.0.2'

RUN <<EOT bash
  set -ex
  curl -L --retry 3 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 2 --fail-with-body -o /tmp/curl-impersonate.tar.gz https://github.com/lexiforest/curl-impersonate/releases/download/${CURL_IMPERSONATE_VERSION}/curl-impersonate-${CURL_IMPERSONATE_VERSION}.x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
  tar -xzf /tmp/curl-impersonate.tar.gz -C /usr/local/bin --no-same-owner
  curl -L --retry 3 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 2 --fail-with-body -o /tmp/libcurl-impersonate.tar.gz https://github.com/lexiforest/curl-impersonate/releases/download/${CURL_IMPERSONATE_VERSION}/libcurl-impersonate-${CURL_IMPERSONATE_VERSION}.x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
  tar -xzf /tmp/libcurl-impersonate.tar.gz -C /tmp --no-same-owner
  mv /tmp/libcurl-impersonate* /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/
  rm -f /tmp/*
  ldconfig
EOT

ENV CURL_IMPERSONATE=chrome136
ENV LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcurl-impersonate.so.4.8.0
```

title: Impersonate http/3 fingerprints
body: It's expected that http/3 can be fingerprinted using the settings frame and window_update etc., just like http/2. We should check and implement the same behavior as browsers when using http/3. It has been verified that curl and browser differ in the settings frames. Here is a [blog post explaining the details of http3 fingerprints](https://impersonate.pro/blog/http3-fingerprints). We have created [a simple API](https://fp.impersonate.pro/api/http3) showcasing the differences in http/3 fingerprints: curl: firefox: chrome:

title: I need help! Differences between Shell Script and node-libcurl
body:
Thank you for the effort put in for this project!



I have a question to ask. The local shell script can retrieve data, but node-libcurl cannot retrieve data.
Environment: The system version Ubuntu24.04LTS runs on a WIN11 VMWare virtual machine.
Target site: AKM site


What did I do?
I have locally compiled the latest version 0.9.5 of curl delegate and obtained the curl chrome131 shell script. Due to the fact that the project will generate the libcurl-imposte-chrome.so file after compilation, I installed the node-libcurl as source code and compiled it together with the generated libcurl-imposte-chrome.so file.


My test:
1. Copy the curl command of the website, and then simulate the request using curl chrome131 in the terminal, and find that the data has been obtained.
2. I converted the complete curl command into node libcwrl code, but found that I couldn't get the data.
3. I converted the curl command from another AKM site into node libcwrl code and found that I could retrieve the data. I don't understand why one site can bypass TLS while another cannot.

title: The install target is missing
body:
Once built it needs to be installed in order to be useful for curl_cffi.

FYI: Builds can't download files in package builders for security reasons. For this reason curl_cffi should be able to use the pre-installed curl-impersonate binaries when available.

The above is true on all platforms, not just FreeBSD. Package builders don't allow any downloads during the build process.

title: The binary links with the external libnghttp2.so due to the incorrect link line
body:
When the external libnghttp2.so is installed the src/.libs/curl-impersonate-chrome binary is linked with it instead of the bundled static library.

This is because of this argument:
> configure: using LIBS: -lnghttp2

The link line should use the full path to the bundled static library instead.

title: Observing differences in the fingerprint between chrome131 impersonate and chrome 132
body:
**The question**

We have chrome v131 impersonate support on curl-cffi with `chrome131` for desktop (Mac, Windows) and `chrome131_android` for Mobile devices.
I was verifying my chrome browsers on mac and on android device and found that Google has updated their chrome browser versions to chrome v132 on desktop and mobile.

As far as my understanding goes, the `ja3n` hash will remain the same for a given browser version. Correct?

As per https://tls.browserleaks.com/json:

- The ja3n hash for _chrome131 impersonate_ is:
```
"ja3n_hash": "dee19b855b658c6aa0f575eda2525e19",
"ja3n_text": "771,4865-4866-4867-49195-49199-49196-49200-52393-52392-49171-49172-156-157-47-53,0-5-10-11-13-16-18-23-27-35-43-45-51-17513-65037-65281,4588-29-23-24,0"
```

- The ja3n hash for _chrome131_android impersonate_ is:
```
"ja3n_hash": "473f0e7c0b6a0f7b049072f4e683068b",
"ja3n_text": "771,4865-4866-4867-49195-49199-49196-49200-52393-52392-49171-49172-156-157-47-53,0-5-10-11-13-16-18-23-27-35-43-45-51-17513-65037-65281,29-23-24,0"
```

- On my _Mac OS_ chrome browser, I observe the following ja3n fingerprint for _chrome v132_:
```
"ja3n_hash": "8e19337e7524d2573be54efb2b0784c9",
"ja3n_text": "771,4865-4866-4867-49195-49199-49196-49200-52393-52392-49171-49172-156-157-47-53,0-5-10-11-13-16-18-23-27-35-43-45-51-17613-65037-65281,4588-29-23-24,0"
```

- On my _Android_ device chrome browser, I observe the following ja3n fingerprint for _chrome v132_:
```
"ja3n_hash": "8e19337e7524d2573be54efb2b0784c9",
"ja3n_text": "771,4865-4866-4867-49195-49199-49196-49200-52393-52392-49171-49172-156-157-47-53,0-5-10-11-13-16-18-23-27-35-43-45-51-17613-65037-65281,4588-29-23-24,0"
```
Following are my questions:
- ja3n hash will remain the same for a given browser version. Correct?
- Is the data available on https://tls.browserleaks.com/json correct and can it be trusted?
- It appears to me that the chrome fingerprint for v132 has changed from the fingerprint for chrome v131 both for Desktop and Mobile. Is this not the case?
-  If it has, would we be able to expect a new chrome v132 impersonate support for Desktop and Mobile?
- If my understanding is incorrect, how can I obtain the `ja3n` string for a device? I do not see anything related to ja3n using Wireshark and Wireshark is also not usable with android devices.

**Versions**

If it's related to a specific environment, paste your env info here.

 - curl_cffi version [0.8.0b7]

title: Updating browser target naming conventions
body:
In the past, the targets are named as `browserVersion[OS]`, e.g. `chrome131`, `safari18_0_ios`. It is somewhat not consistant and can be confusing, especially for safari targets.

In the future, I would like to change the convention to `browser_version[_os]`. For example:

- `chrome_131`
- `edge_124_windows`
- `safari_172_ios`, Note that safari versions are compacted to a single number for consistency.
- `chrome_131_android`

With the new pattern, the string can be parsed as `version.split("_")`.

Since this is a breaking change, the update will happen with a major version bump, i.e. `v1.x`. And all the old versions will be aliased.

title: Incorrect behavior when aborting download in v0.8
body:
### Problem

libcurl provides a `WRITEFUNCTION` [option](https://curl.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION.html) to process response chunks. Its behavior is to abort the download if returned integer is not equal to the length of passed chunk.

> Your callback should return the number of bytes actually taken care of. If that amount differs from the amount passed to your callback function, it signals an error condition to the library. This causes the transfer to get aborted and the libcurl function used returns [CURLE_WRITE_ERROR](https://curl.se/libcurl/c/libcurl-errors.html#CURLEWRITEERROR).

It looks like instead of `E_WRITE_ERROR`, latest `libcurl-impersonate` is returning `E_RECV_ERROR` which breaks the abort functionality and makes it impossible to differentiate between server side receive errors/timeouts and on-purpose aborts.

### Test Case

Following is the minimal test case with `pycurl` that can be used to reproduce this:
```
import pycurl

print(pycurl.version)

url = 'https://bit.ly/4874LxR'


def abort_write(_):
    '''
    Abort writing response body.
    '''
    return -1


curl = pycurl.Curl()
curl.setopt(pycurl.URL, url.encode('utf-8'))
curl.setopt(pycurl.FOLLOWLOCATION, 1)
curl.setopt(pycurl.WRITEFUNCTION, abort_write)
curl.perform()
curl.close()

```

### Results

Use `LD_PRELOAD` to load `libcurl-impersonate 0.8.0` and run the test. Error `56 (E_RECV_ERROR)` will return:

```
$ LD_PRELOAD=/local/lib/libcurl-0.8.0.so CURL_IMPERSONATE=chrome124 python pycurl_test.py 

PycURL/7.45.3 libcurl/8.7.0-DEV BoringSSL zlib/1.3 brotli/1.1.0 zstd/1.5.6 nghttp2/1.63.0

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/ubuntu/pycurl_test.py", line 22, in <module>
    curl.perform()

pycurl.error: (56, 'Failure writing output to destination, passed 1369 returned -1')
```

I tried the same test case with `libcurl-impersonate 0.7.0b1` built with older `libcurl v8.5` and it passed:
```
$ LD_PRELOAD=/local/lib/libcurl-0.7.0b1.so CURL_IMPERSONATE=chrome124 python pycurl_test.py 

PycURL/7.45.3 libcurl/8.5.0 BoringSSL zlib/1.3 brotli/1.0.9 zstd/1.5.6 nghttp2/1.56.0

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/ubuntu/pycurl_test.py", line 22, in <module>
    curl.perform()

pycurl.error: (23, 'Failure writing output to destination')
```

Error `23 (E_WRITE_ERROR)` is the expected code, which allows client to handle on-purpose aborts and process the result. Something got broken in latest impersonation patch or maybe in libcurl v8.7.1 itself. Strangely though, version API returns 8.7.1 as `8.7.0-DEV` implying that it is not stable.

title: Chrome 'priority' header
body:
Hello,

I've noticed that the priority header gets sent, however comparing it to browser requests (using webhook.site for example to get the request headers) shows that they do not in fact send it. 
According to [this article ](https://chromestatus.com/feature/5109106573049856) the header itself doesn't get sent.

No clue if that would break stuff in the impersonation level, however I've just bumped into issue with one site with the request headers being too big (http 431) and this might be a reason for such issues with servers that support up to http11 and not http2 and 3 which use the priority header.

title: libcurl.dll x86_64 exception occasionally
body:
Has anyone encountered occasional exceptions with the libcurl.dll library in the Windows x86_64 version? Through debugging and analysis, it was found that in the function `void Curl_resolver_cancel(struct Curl_easy *data) { destroy_async_data(&data->conn->resolve_async); },` the data->conn is already null. It seems that the following function is called twice:`/*
 * Curl_detach_connection() removes the given transfer from the connection.
 *
 * This is the only function that should clear data->conn. This will
 * occasionally be called with the data->conn pointer already cleared.
 */
void Curl_detach_connection(struct Curl_easy *data);`
The comment within this function also indicates that there may be occasional multiple clearings of data->conn. In actual use, this occasionally triggers exceptions, and there is no 100% reproducible method found. However, after switching to using the c-ares library, the problem has not been observed so far.

title: Unknown CMake command `openssl_check_symbol_exists` for `USE_ECH` option
body:
I tried build with CMake but got error (Unknown CMake command "openssl_check_symbol_exists".) because of `USE_ECH` option. If I move ECH option snippet to below `openssl_check_symbol_exists` macro, it fixes.

Here it is new patch about ECH option snippet to fix the problem.
```diff
diff --git a/CMakeLists.txt b/CMakeLists.txt
index a54c2ff..9b23a59 100644
--- a/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -671,6 +671,29 @@ if(USE_OPENSSL OR USE_WOLFSSL)
   endif()
 endif()
 
+option(USE_ECH "Enable ECH support" OFF)
+if(USE_ECH)
+  if(USE_OPENSSL OR USE_WOLFSSL)
+    # Be sure that the OpenSSL/wolfSSL library actually supports ECH.
+    if(NOT DEFINED HAVE_ECH)
+      if(USE_OPENSSL AND HAVE_BORINGSSL)
+        openssl_check_symbol_exists(SSL_set1_ech_config_list "openssl/ssl.h" HAVE_ECH)
+      elseif(USE_OPENSSL)
+        openssl_check_symbol_exists(SSL_ech_set1_echconfig "openssl/ech.h" HAVE_ECH)
+      elseif(USE_WOLFSSL)
+        openssl_check_symbol_exists(wolfSSL_CTX_GenerateEchConfig "wolfssl/options.h;wolfssl/ssl.h" HAVE_ECH)
+      endif()
+    endif()
+    if(NOT HAVE_ECH)
+      message(FATAL_ERROR "ECH support missing in OpenSSL/BoringSSL/wolfSSL")
+    else()
+      message("ECH enabled.")
+    endif()
+  else()
+    message(FATAL_ERROR "ECH requires ECH-enablded OpenSSL, BoringSSL or wolfSSL")
+  endif()
+endif()
+
 option(USE_NGHTTP2 "Use nghttp2 library" OFF)
 if(USE_NGHTTP2)
   find_package(NGHTTP2 REQUIRED)
```

title: Compile Linux releases with `zig cc`
body:
The Zig compiler supports building C and C++ code with `zig cc` and `zig c++`, since it uses clang internally. With clang, [cross] compiling to x86_64, aarch64, and arm32 is possible with the same toolchain, and even cross compiling to Windows/MacOS if desired. Additionally, Zig allows targeting a specific glibc release, which would make it easier to pin to glibc 2.17 (for manylinux2014 compliance) without using old distro containers.

I've had success in my [Portable Python](https://github.com/bjia56/portable-python) project using Zig to compile all of CPython and its dependencies against glibc 2.17, so I think it should be possible to do the same here.

I was wondering if it was possible for you to integrate libcurl-impersonate into a native [Node.js addon](https://nodejs.org/api/addons.html) so it works in JS out-of-the-box, without the long and tedious process of building [node-libcurl](https://github.com/JCMais/node-libcurl) with the impersonate patch.

title: Set MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET to be the earliest supported version
body:
The MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET env var controls which minimum MacOS version the compilation will target. For arm64, the minimum possible version is always MacOS 11.0 (even if the env var is set to be lower), but for x86_64 the version could be even lower (e.g. 10.15).

Without setting this env var, libcurl may not work on users running an older MacOS than the gh actions worker - e.g. in this issue: https://github.com/jeffreydwalter/arlo/pull/205

title: Conform builds to manylinux2014 glibc standards
body:
Restructures the Linux build to do the compiling inside Centos 7 Docker containers published by the manylinux team for x86_64 and aarch64, and a container maintained by myself for armv7l. This ensures that the resulting binaries target glibc 2.17, which is required by manylinux2014.

I was unable to get cross compilation working, since devtoolset-10 does not appear to provide cross compilers. Using the system cross compiler, which is gcc 4.8.5, is unable to properly build some of the dependencies. Thus, QEMU emulation is used to build "native" aarch64 and armv7l binaries. A full cache-less build takes roughly two hours.

Other changes:
- Split out the Linux and MacOS build jobs
- Add patches to BoringSSL for it to build on old Centos 7
- Add ability to parallelize builds
- Set an env var to target MacOS SDK 10.15 (haven't inspected the binaries to see if this works yet)

Needed for https://github.com/yifeikong/curl_cffi/pull/186

title: Recheck boringssl's `OPENSSL_NO_ASM` for Windows build

Useful links: 

1. https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/9440
2. https://github.com/mit-plv/fiat-crypto
